flawed_step: Step 5: the claim that in a 3-coloring of G−v, Kempe-chain recoloring can always make the independent neighbourhood N(v) use at most 2 colours. Triangle-freeness only makes N(v) an independent set. It does not stop its vertices from getting all 3 colours, and Kempe swaps can fail when the chains are linked.
counterexample: The Chvátal graph: 12 vertices, 4-regular (so Δ=4), triangle-free, with chromatic number 4. This is a standard known fact; it was not recomputed here. It is the smallest triangle-free 4-regular graph that is 4-chromatic.
assessment_summary:
Proof attempt, with a judgement on each step:
1. Let G be simple and triangle-free with Δ(G) ≤ 4. We may assume G is connected, since the chromatic number is the maximum over the components. — Justified.
2. By Brooks' theorem χ(G) ≤ Δ ≤ 4, because G is not K5 (K5 has triangles) and not an odd cycle with Δ > 2. — Justified, but it only gives 4 colours, not 3.
3. Take a counterexample G with the fewest vertices. Every proper subgraph is 3-colourable. — Justified as a setup, if the statement is true; otherwise the argument must fail somewhere later.
4. Minimality forces δ(G) ≥ 3: a vertex of degree ≤ 2 can be deleted, the rest 3-coloured, and the vertex coloured last. — Justified.
5. Pick v of degree 3 or 4 and 3-colour G−v. N(v) is independent because G is triangle-free. Claim: Kempe (a,b)-chain swaps can always reduce N(v) to at most 2 colours, freeing a colour for v. — NOT justified. Being independent does not limit how many colours N(v) uses. With degree 4, one colour appears twice on N(v), and swaps can fail when the chains are linked, as in Kempe's flawed four-colour argument. No property of triangle-free graphs with Δ ≤ 4 rules this out.
6. Conclude that v can be coloured, contradicting minimality, so G is 3-colourable. — Not justified, because it depends on step 5.

The failure in step 5 is real, not just a gap in this proof. The Chvátal graph (12 vertices, 4-regular, triangle-free) has chromatic number 4. This is a known result that I did not recompute. It meets both readings of 'maximum degree 4' and cannot be 3-coloured, so the statement is false. The best general bound here is the 4 colours from Brooks' theorem.
